Automatic two-level calendar variation model

Source: R/lunarcast.R
lunarcast.Rd

Fits a regression with ARIMA errors in which moving holidays enter through window regressors and may have a different effect at every occurrence, and selects the whole specification automatically.

Usage

lunarcast(
  y,
  holidays,
  effect = "auto",
  window = "auto",
  grid = list(pre = c(0, 3, 7, 14, 28), post = c(0, 3, 7, 14)),
  level2 = "auto",
  k = 3,
  lambda = 0,
  share = c("level", "linear"),
  trend = c("auto", "none", "deterministic", "stochastic"),
  season = c("auto", "none", "dummy", "fourier", "stochastic"),
  select = c("cv", "aicc"),
  cv_years = 5,
  cv_rule = c("1se", "min"),
  outliers = FALSE,
  cval = 3.5,
  xreg = NULL,
  min_events = 6,
  ...
)

Arguments

y

Monthly or quarterly `ts`.

holidays

Named list of `Date` vectors, e.g. `list(adha = holiday_dates("idul_adha"))`.

effect

`"auto"`, `"constant"` or `"two-level"`, or a named list.

window

`"auto"` or `c(pre, post)` in days, or a named list.

grid

List with candidate `pre` and `post` offsets (days, >= 0).

level2

`"auto"`, `"mean"`, `"wmean"` (precision-weighted mean), `"rw"`, `"ses"`, `"holt"` (damped) or a fixed log effect, or a named list.

k

Number of recent occurrences used by `"mean"` and `"wmean"`.

lambda

Box-Cox parameter; `0` (default) gives multiplicative effects, `NULL` none.

share

`"level"` maps window shares to the log scale (only for `lambda = 0`); `"linear"` uses them as they are.

trend

`"auto"`, `"none"`, `"deterministic"` or `"stochastic"`.

season

`"auto"`, `"none"`, `"dummy"`, `"fourier"` or `"stochastic"`.

select

`"cv"` compares the candidate structures (deterministic and stochastic trend, each with no, Fourier, dummy or stochastic seasonality) by one-year-ahead forecasts from `cv_years` origins one year apart at the end of the sample; `"aicc"` chooses the trend by KPSS tests and the seasonality by AICc.

cv_years

Number of forecast origins for `select = "cv"`.

cv_rule

`"1se"` (default) takes the simplest structure whose CV-RMSE is within one standard error (across forecast origins) of the smallest; `"min"` takes the structure with the smallest CV-RMSE.

outliers

If `TRUE`, additive outliers, level shifts and temporary changes are detected outside the periods of two-level holidays.

cval

Critical |t| value for outliers.

xreg

Optional extra regressors with at least `length(y) + h` rows (rows beyond `length(y)` are used for forecasting).

min_events

Minimum number of occurrences for a two-level effect.

...

Passed to [forecast::auto.arima()].

Value

An object of class `"lunarcast"` with, among others, the fitted ARIMA model (`fit`), the selected windows (`window`), effect types (`effect`) and structure (`structure`), the occurrence effects (`effects`, see [holiday_effects()]), the level-2 rules (`level2`) and the cross-validation table (`cv`).

Model

On the log scale (`lambda = 0`), with \(z_t = \log y_t\), $$z_t = \sum_h \sum_j \alpha_{hj}\,\tilde w_{hj,t} + \mathbf{x}_t^\top \boldsymbol\beta + N_t,$$ where \(w_{hj,t}\) is the share of the window \([D_{hj} + a_h, D_{hj} + b_h]\) around occurrence \(j\) of holiday \(h\) that falls in period \(t\), mapped to the log scale by \(\tilde w = \log\{1 + (e^{\alpha} - 1) w\} / \alpha\); \(\mathbf{x}_t\) holds the trend, seasonal and outlier regressors and \(N_t\) is an ARIMA process. With a *constant* effect \(\alpha_{hj} = \alpha_h\); with a *two-level* effect every occurrence has its own \(\alpha_{hj}\) (level 1) and the effect of the next occurrence is forecast from the sequence of past effects (level 2). See `vignette("theory", package = "lunarcast")`.

Automatic specification

(1) a preliminary trend type by KPSS tests; (2) constant versus two-level effect and (3) the window of every holiday by AICc on a grid (coordinate-wise, linear window shares, non-seasonal ARIMA errors); (4) optionally outliers outside two-level holiday periods; (5) the trend and seasonal structure by calendar-aware cross-validation with a one-standard-error rule (`select = "cv"`) or by KPSS tests and AICc (`select = "aicc"`); (6) the final ARIMA order by [forecast::auto.arima()] (for stochastic seasonality the seasonal order comes from a small grid); (7) the level-2 rule by one-step-ahead cross-validation on the sequence of occurrence effects.

See also

[forecast.lunarcast()], [holiday_effects()], [calvar_classic()] for the classical model and [rolling_origin()] for evaluation.

Examples

hol <- list(adha = holiday_dates("idul_adha"),
            fitri = holiday_dates("idul_fitri"))
# fixed windows and structure keep the example fast
fit <- lunarcast(sapi, hol,
                 window = list(adha = c(-3, 7), fitri = c(-28, 3)),
                 effect = list(adha = "two-level", fitri = "constant"),
                 trend = "stochastic", season = "none")
fit
